text: My cat was misgendered This sweet baby came onto my porch demanding food roughly 2 months ago. We got her to the vet for checks and vaccines multiple times, did bloodwork, checked body temperature, the works. I asked the vet if my cat is a girl or a boy, told the vet that the cat is a stray and I don’t know its background. I got reassured that she’s a girl, so we finally scheduled her to get a spay. We got her inside for the night, fasted her, prepared everything carefully for our little princess, brought her in and waited anxiously at home for the call to go collect her. The surgeon personally called me, asked for my name, confirmed that she’s my cat, told me that something happened, it sometimes happens and he’s sorry. I got so anxious I was sweating and trembling thinking that my cat didn’t make it, but I got told that my little princess is in fact a prince. Turns out he was neutered as a kitten and has a very small wee wee. I am still recovering after 2 days, and my poor little guy got a full abdominal surgery he didn’t need and I feel so guilty. I had my suspicions and looked at his face multiple times thinking he looks like a boy, but ultimately trusted the vet. He doesn’t like it inside and cries so much for the outdoors life and he has to be kept prisoner because of a surgery he didn’t need. Beyond shock, I feel just so sad for him. I feel so guilt. Let this be your sign to double check if you have doubts and listen to your gut. TL;DR: The stray cat that landed on my porch was pronounced female by the vet, took her for a spay, the abdominal surgery revealed he’s in fact a neutered male.

I think i accidentally adopted the most affectionate cat So, just over a week ago, I adopted a 6-year-old cat called Duchess, now renamed Boo. I was specifically looking for an older rescue cat rather than a kitten, and she seemed like a good fit. The funny thing is, she was described as a bit of a diva, independent, and apparently aggressive. Naturally, I prepared myself for a long settling-in period, plenty of hiding, and having to earn her trust over weeks or months. Boo apparently didn’t get that memo. The first few days, she mostly hid under my bed or in her carrier, which I expected. I gave her space, let her approach me on her terms, and never forced her to interact with me. Fast-forward to now, and I genuinely think I’ve accidentally adopted a tiny, furry Velcro creature. She: Climbs onto my bed completely of her own accord and settles right next to me. Makes biscuits on me while purring so loudly you’d think she had an engine installed. Leaves to get food, then comes straight back to me. Follows me around the house and sometimes tries to lead me upstairs when she wants something. Headbutts my hand repeatedly if I dare to stop petting her. Rubs her face against me, licks me, and leans into every bit of fuss she can get. Has now decided that my lap is an acceptable place to spend her time. Today, she spent around 10 minutes making biscuits on me while purring like an absolute machine before settling down. She doesn’t even need me to call her over anymore. I’ll just be lying there, and she’ll come and curl up beside me herself. The best part is that she still has her little independent-cat moments, but apparently being independent means she can choose to be attached to me at any given moment. I went into this expecting to slowly gain the trust of a potentially difficult cat. Instead, I’m barely two weeks in, and she’s already acting like she’s known me her entire life. Obviously, she’s still settling in, and I know she’ll have her own boundaries and off days. But I’m genuinely baffled by the difference between the description I was given and the cat I’m actually living with. I’m starting to wonder whether she was genuinely aggressive in her previous home, whether she was misunderstood, or whether she’s just decided that I’m her person. Either way, I appear to have been adopted by Boo. TL;DR: Adopted a cat described as aggressive and independent, prepared for months of earning her trust, and somehow ended up with a purring, biscuit-making, hand-bunting lap cat who follows me around and comes back for cuddles after eating. I think I’ve been conned, and honestly, I’m delighted

New kitten is respectful and responsive to resident cats boundary setting.. RC frequently hisses and bats but there hasn’t been any “cat fights”. However, I can sense RC is not happy about the kitten overall. Some weird patterns with litterbox- peeing but only pooping every 36 hours or so, which is unusual for her. She will only poop if kitten is shut away. Today, before I left, RC stepped in and out of litter a couple of times and even sat in it for a couple of minutes only producing a small pee. I’m worried that we are at a stand still and that I’m going to have to give the kitten back due to it not being a suitable match for my RC, which would break my heart.
